clue.text: Taunt honourable man displaying nervous symptom

parts.note: to taunt someone is to twit them, an old verb for teasing
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order whose members are honourable men and women

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a dignitary, who shows signs of nervousness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taunt' looks like a verb in a sentence, but it supplies the first piece; CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A tic or small involuntary jerk of a muscle is a classic sign of nerves.

clue.text: Soften after one day in London

indicators.note: one day placed in London means the letters go inside the word for the capital

parts.note: Londoners call their city 'town', as in going up to town
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something mellows after a day spent in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Town' is a traditional British way of referring to London.
explanation.definitionFit: To moderate or make less harsh is to soften, as with language or colour.

clue.text: Stone hollowed out by giant oil spill

indicators.note: an oil spill spreads the liquid about, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A huge oil spill wears a hollow in a rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spill' looks like part of the oil disaster but signals rearranging GIANT OIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A gem carved with a sunken design is an engraved stone, the opposite of a cameo.

clue.text: Brag, and cause many a set-to

definitions.meaning: the idiom 'a ... to pluck' means a grievance to settle, a cause of quarrels

explanation.definitionFit: Boasting loudly is crowing, and the black bird figures in the idiom about a quarrel to settle with someone.

clue.text: An article on south Carolina is vitriolic

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece written on another follows it, so the article phrase comes after the state letters

parts.note: C abbreviates Carolina, as in the US state codes SC and NC
an article is an object or item, a thing

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about South Carolina is bitterly hostile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a newspaper piece, but here it just means an object. 'On' places A THING after S and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe bitterly harsh, cutting criticism, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Governmental guidelines need structure

definitions.meaning: a nation's founding body of laws and principles
a person's physical makeup or build

explanation.definitionFit: A state's fundamental laws, and the bodily makeup of a person, share this one word.

clue.text: Tidy the top border

definitions.meaning: to cut back hair or a hedge neatly
a decorative edging on clothing or furniture

explanation.definitionFit: Cutting hair neatly and a decorative edging on clothes are both this word.

clue.text: Peaceable part of Yorkshire — nice little backwater

indicators.note: only a part of the following words is taken, a run of letters spanning them

explanation.surface: A quiet, pleasant backwater in one corner of Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'YorkshIRE NICe'; 'nice little backwater' completes the peaceful picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Promoting peace and conciliation is the meaning of this rare adjective from the Greek for peace.

clue.text: Understand how to make a dirndl skirt

definitions.text: how to make a dirndl skirt
definitions.meaning: a dirndl skirt is made full by drawing the fabric into folds at the waist

explanation.definitionFit: To infer something is to deduce it, and dressmakers pull fabric into small folds to make a full dirndl skirt.

clue.text: One taken in by unacceptable concept

indicators.note: something taken in by another is held inside it, so the numeral goes within the phrase for unacceptable

parts.note: something unacceptable is 'not on' in British idiom
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Someone is fooled by an idea nobody will accept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on' is British slang for unacceptable; 'taken in by' looks like being deceived but signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea or belief held in the mind is a synonym for a concept.

clue.text: Very poor ending — it must be rewritten

indicators.note: writing the two words out again in a different order is the instruction to rearrange their letters

explanation.surface: A writer is told the dreadful final scene of the story needs redoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very poor' reads as a verdict on the ending, but it is the definition; the letters of ENDING IT are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A destitute person, lacking money and the necessities of life, is extremely poor.

clue.text: Inferring that army VIP is in Gateshead

parts.note: a general is a senior army officer
taken as written
taken as written
read as Gate's head, the first letter of the word gate

explanation.surface: An army chief is said to be in a town on Tyneside.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead is a town in north-east England; split as 'Gates head' it gives the head of 'Gates', the letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing broad conclusions from particular instances is a kind of deduction.

clue.text: Ideal lodgings for archaeologists

parts.note: the word for rented rooms in Britain is also the word for excavation sites, so it suits people who dig

explanation.surface: A joke about where diggers of the past should stay.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage this word is informal for rented rooms; archaeologists also work on excavations called by the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for rented rooms coincides with the term for archaeological excavations.

clue.text: Cleric is detailed to find a page

indicators.note: to detail something here is to cut off its tail, so the final letter of the clergyman goes

parts.note: a rector is a parish clergyman in the Church of England

explanation.surface: A clergyman is assigned the task of locating a page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' reads as 'assigned a task', but it means 'with its tail removed': RECTOR loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The right-hand page of an open book, or the front of a leaf, is a specific page.

clue.text: Summon by name

definitions.meaning: to summon someone to appear in court is to issue a legal citation
to name something as an example or authority is to quote it

explanation.definitionFit: A court may formally call a person to appear, and a writer may mention a source as an authority: both are this verb.

clue.text: Gong summons many into dinner, perhaps

indicators.note: one thing put into another goes inside it, so the numeral sits within the dinner word

parts.note: dinner is an example of a meal
D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number

explanation.surface: A gong calls everyone in to dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gong' summoning to dinner is the surface, but a gong is British slang for a medal; D (500) is 'many'.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a decoration or award given for service or bravery.

clue.text: Living with a German in Bulgaria

indicators.note: the German word goes in the letters for Bulgaria, placed between them

parts.note: BG is the international code for Bulgaria
ein is German for a

explanation.surface: Someone lives in Bulgaria alongside a German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A German' means the German word for 'a', EIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Existence or life, as in 'human' creature, is the noun sense.

clue.text: Coward could get it if the weather changes

indicators.note: when the weather changes it alters, so these words are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone timid might receive something if conditions turn.
explanation.walkthrough: A white feather was given to men seen as cowards, notably in Britain during the First World War; 'changes' signals rearranging IF THE WEATHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Handing a man a pale plume was a traditional accusation of cowardice.

clue.text: Diane's directive results in chaos

parts.note: Di is a short form of Diane, so Diane's is Di's
an order is a directive or command

explanation.surface: Diane's instructions lead to mayhem.
explanation.walkthrough: Di is a common short form of the name Diane.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of confusion and lack of order is chaos.

clue.text: Hired ten builders, despite lacking credit

indicators.note: builders put things together anew, so these letters are reassembled in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A firm took on ten builders even though it had no money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Builders' looks like the people hired, but it signals rearranging HIRED TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Being overdrawn, with debts rather than funds, is being without credit.

clue.text: Heed advice to settle bills with civility

parts.note: telling someone to pay is advice to settle their bills
attention, as in paying attentions, means courteous consideration

explanation.surface: A recommendation to clear one's debts politely.
explanation.walkthrough: Attention in the sense of courteous care, as in 'attentions' paid to someone, supplies the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: To take heed is to listen and concentrate carefully, the same as this phrase.

clue.text: Pole was sick on being caught

parts.note: N stands for north, one of the earth's poles
ailed means was ill

explanation.surface: A Polish man fell ill on being arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person, but it is the North Pole, N.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, to catch or arrest someone is to pin them down, as with a fixing spike.

clue.text: A loose lady in the family

parts.note: to loose a knot is to untie it

explanation.surface: A promiscuous woman among one's relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose lady' suggests a promiscuous woman, but 'loose' is a verb meaning to untie.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's sister is a female relative, and this is the affectionate form.

clue.text: Lords and ladies need a drink

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Aristocrats want something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lords and ladies' looks like the nobility, but it is a common name for the wild arum, a woodland plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Lords-and-ladies, or cuckoo-pint, is a folk name for a woodland plant of this genus.

clue.text: Check it is in, son

indicators.note: the word it is in son, meaning placed within that word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A parent asks a boy whether something is in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' looks like an instruction to the son, but it is the definition: to check is to suppress.
explanation.definitionFit: To curb or suppress something is to restrain it, the sense of this phrasal verb.

clue.text: Ex-student returning quietly? Rubbish!

indicators.note: something returning comes back, so the ex-student's letters are read backwards

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil of a school
SH is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A former pupil comes back softly, and someone scoffs at it.
explanation.walkthrough: OB, old boy, is a British term for a former pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an informal exclamation meaning nonsense.

clue.text: Excels in gaining sporting awards

definitions.meaning: to cap something is to outdo or top it
a cap is awarded to a player chosen for a national team

explanation.definitionFit: Outdoing or topping something, and the hats awarded for playing for one's country, share this word.

clue.text: Exam taken by foursome in Virginia

indicators.note: the numeral group goes in the state's letters, sitting between them

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
IV is the Roman numeral for four

explanation.surface: A test is sat by a group of four in Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: IV is the Roman numeral for four.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral examination, especially at university, is called by this Latin term.

clue.text: Libertine reluctant to go to a s. American port

parts.note: loth means unwilling or reluctant
Rio de Janeiro is a South American port, often called Rio

explanation.surface: A rake is unwilling to travel to a port in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: Loth is a variant spelling of loath, reluctant.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who seduces women is a rake or seducer, named from a character in an old play.

clue.text: Austrian children are more considerate

definitions.meaning: the comparative of kind, meaning more thoughtful

explanation.definitionFit: German speakers in Austria call their offspring by this word, and it is also the comparative form of an adjective meaning thoughtful.

clue.text: Groom needs time to prepare horses for it

parts.note: to groom someone is to dress them, make them neat
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A stable hand needs time to get the horses ready for an event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' suggests a stable hand, but it is a verb meaning to dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Horses are trained for this equestrian discipline of precise movements, so it is what one readies them for.

clue.text: A bishop retired when obstructed

annotationWithheld.why: A bishop retired when obstructed (6): the only parse is A + RR inside BED, with 'retired' (in bed) giving BED and also signalling the container, one word doing two jobs
